key_insight: MorphContrast uses tissue morphology to guide AI prediction of five-year colorectal cancer survival from whole-slide images, with prognostic signals extending beyond tumor tissue.
clinical_relevance: This prognosis study—not drug discovery—could inform future risk-stratification research but does not establish clinical utility or guide treatment.
method: Combines morphology-aware contrastive learning with gated-attention multiple-instance pooling.
Contrasts tissue patches within and across patients, using outcome-discordant, morphology-matched patches as hard negatives.
Adds diversity regularization to discourage representational collapse.
evidence_signal: Retrospective analysis used TCGA (n=562), Alliance/CALGB 89803 (n=424), and external SurGen data (n=218); single-model/ensemble AUCs were 0.642/0.70 internally and 0.669/0.678 externally.
watch_item: Modest external discrimination and post hoc ensemble evaluation warrant prospective validation before clinical use.
paper_title: Morphology-aware deep learning predicts colorectal cancer survival from whole-slide images
